viewsWelcome.contents:
Open an XSD or WSDL file to see its schemas, types, elements, operations and services here.
[Open Sample Schema](command:xsdAtlas.openSampleSchema)
[Open Sample WSDL](command:xsdAtlas.openSampleWsdl)
[Getting Started Guide](command:xsdAtlas.openWalkthrough)

Compare two versions of a schema (Pro, included in the free 14-day trial). Every change is listed as breaking, non-breaking or documentation only.
[Compare With Another File](command:xsdAtlas.compareFiles)
[Compare With Git Revision](command:xsdAtlas.compareRevisions)
[Compare Two Folders](command:xsdAtlas.compareFolders)

walkthroughs.title: Get started with XSD Atlas
walkthroughs.description: Open a sample schema, read its structure, jump between definitions, build a sample XML document and compare two schema versions with the free 14-day Pro trial.

steps.title: Open a sample schema
steps.description:
XSD Atlas reads XML Schema (XSD) and WSDL 1.1 and 2.0 files. Open the short invented samples to follow along, or open one of your own files.
[Open Sample Schema](command:xsdAtlas.openSampleSchema)
[Open Sample WSDL](command:xsdAtlas.openSampleWsdl)

steps.title: Read the outline and hover a type
steps.description:
The XSD Atlas view lists imports, elements, types, groups and attributes, or for a WSDL the messages, operations, bindings and services. Hover a type name to see its definition, base types, facets and documentation.
[Show the Outline](command:workbench.view.extension.xsdAtlas)

steps.title: Jump to definitions and check problems
steps.description:
F12 on a type or element reference opens its definition, also across imports and includes; Shift+F12 lists every use. Broken references, duplicate names and invalid facets show up in the Problems view with a stable code.
[Check Current File](command:xsdAtlas.checkFile)

steps.title: Create a sample XML document
steps.description:
Pick a global element and get a minimal document with every required element and values that satisfy the facets.
[Create Sample XML](command:xsdAtlas.sampleXml)

steps.title: Compare two versions (Pro trial)
steps.description:
Open version 2 of the sample, then compare it with version 1: each change is classified as breaking, non-breaking or documentation. The first Pro command starts a free 14-day trial on this computer; no key, account or network is needed.
[Open Sample Schema Version 2](command:xsdAtlas.openSampleSchemaV2)
[Compare Schema With Another File](command:xsdAtlas.compareFiles)
[Show Licence Status](command:xsdAtlas.licenceStatus)

xsdAtlas.maxFileSizeMB.markdownDescription: Largest file, in megabytes, that is analysed automatically for problems, outline, hovers and navigation. Larger files are checked on demand with **XSD Atlas: Check Current File**, up to 32 MB.

xsdAtlas.maxProblems.markdownDescription: Maximum number of problems shown per file.

xsdAtlas.validateOnType.markdownDescription: Check schema files while you type (after a short pause). When off, files are checked when opened and saved. Files above 2 MB are only checked on save.

xsdAtlas.hover.enabled.markdownDescription: Show the definition of a type, element, attribute or group when the pointer rests on its name.

xsdAtlas.workspace.include.markdownDescription: Glob pattern of the files used for workspace-wide go to definition, find references and the schema inventory.

xsdAtlas.workspace.exclude.markdownDescription: Glob pattern of files and folders that the workspace-wide features skip.

xsdAtlas.workspace.maxFiles.markdownDescription: Largest number of schema files the workspace-wide features read.

xsdAtlas.sample.repeat.markdownDescription: How often **Create Full Sample XML** (Pro) repeats elements that may occur more than once (never more than their maxOccurs).

xsdAtlas.sample.seed.markdownDescription: Seed for the values of **Create Full Sample XML** and **Create SOAP Envelope Samples** (Pro). The same seed and schema give the same document.

xsdAtlas.sample.realisticValues.markdownDescription: In the Pro samples, use values that fit the names of elements and attributes (an e-mail address for `email`, a city for `city`, ...), whenever they also satisfy the facets of the type.

xsdAtlas.export.neutraliseFormulas.markdownDescription: In CSV exports (Pro), put an apostrophe before every cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return, so that a spreadsheet shows it as text instead of running it as a formula. Turn off only when you need the exact values and open the files in a program that does not run formulas.
